messages:
izzy: Trying the browser quickstart (React sample) on localhost. first API call from the client fails with 401 in the console but curl shows 403/billing. i'm confused why the browser shows 401.

pat: can you paste the fetch snippet and the exact browser console error?

izzy: code from App.js:
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REACT_APP_REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hi' })
})
.then(r => r.json()).then(console.log).catch(console.error);
```
browser console: "Failed to load https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate: Request header field authorization is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers in preflight response." then network tab shows an OPTIONS preflight that returned 401 Unauthorized.

billing-bot: NOTE: Org 'izzy-labs' has no active billing profile. Hosted API calls will be blocked until a billing profile is attached.

izzy: curling the endpoint from my laptop (with same key) gives: 403 {"detail":"workspace requires billing"}. so backend says billing, browser shows a preflight 401 with a CORS header issue.

pat: two separate problems interacting: (1) browser preflight is failing before the actual POST so the client sees the preflight error (401) which looks like auth/cors. (2) backend is returning 403 for the POST when called directly because the org needs billing. Several SDKs/guides assume server-side usage or proxying for browser apps.

security-bot: Browser keys are not allowed for production. We recommend using a short-lived token from a backend proxy for client apps. Console also allows configuring CORS origins per org.

izzy: ah ok i was following the README that shows a tiny client-side example. it didn't explicitly call out that you need to either (a) configure the org CORS origins AND have billing enabled, or (b) use a server-side proxy/service key.

devex: action items: (1) clarify quickstart README that the browser sample is only for ephemeral local dev and requires adding localhost to CORS in org console and adding billing for hosted API calls, (2) make the browser sample start a tiny local proxy by default to avoid exposing keys, (3) adjust SDK/browser error mapping so preflight 401/403 surface clearer message like "CORS/preflight failed: check allowed origins and billing".

console-team: we'll add a console hint in the CORS settings page: "If your first browser request errors with 401/403, check billing and that your origin is allowed".

izzy: workaround that worked for me: (1) enable billing on the org, (2) add http://localhost:3000 to CORS origins in console, (3) restart the React dev server so the preflight is reissued. after that the client POST returned 200.

pat: note about restart: many local dev servers cache preflight results; also browsers may cache CORS failures. restarting often forces a fresh OPTIONS. we should mention that in the docs.

billing-bot: Created support ticket S-9876 to help users with trial credits for SSO-created orgs; sometimes trials are not auto-applied for orgs created via SSO providers.

devex: filing RDW-8010 (docs clarifying browser quickstart + CORS + billing), RDW-8011 (sample proxy template), RDW-8012 (SDK: surface preflight+billing combined errors).

console-team: we'll also probe adding a console-level banner for SSO orgs to call out potential trial/credit gaps.

izzy: thanks all  fixed after adding billing + CORS + restart. would've saved me 20 minutes if the quickstart highlighted the flow. closing after tickets created. :raised_hands:
